items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.excerpt: Google Research describes building blocks for AI agents that plan and run real wet-lab biology experiments, grounding agent reasoning in physical lab results toward autonomous labs.

items.title: AI designs working molecular scissors that recognize and cut selected protein targets
items.excerpt: Baker lab (UW) used RFdiffusion2, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold 3 to design cysteine and zinc proteases from scratch; two Nature papers report designs that cut targets such as amyloid-beta and TDP-43, with AI refinement boosting one enzyme ~30-fold.

items.title: Machine learning analysis of gene regulation reveals new dimension of biological variability
items.excerpt: Machine learning applied to allele-specific gene regulation shows the two parental gene copies are often switched on and off out of sync, revealing a new layer of biological variability.

items.title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs hidden patterns inside ultrathin magnets from external fields
items.excerpt: A physics-guided neural approach infers the internal magnetization of nanoscale magnets from the stray fields microscopes can measure, solving an ill-posed inverse problem relevant to spintronic computing.

items.title: LLMs show a human-like double standard when judging others' reasoning
items.excerpt: A study finds large language models judge others' reasoning with a human-like, Bayesian-style double standard, a new probe of machine cognition and bias.

items.title: Researchers dispute whether AI has passed the Turing test
items.excerpt: Researchers debate whether recent results showing chatbots fooling human judges truly mean AI has passed the Turing test, and what the test actually measures.

items.title: Using electronic structure to guide AI in designing new materials
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo researchers extended a leading generative AI materials model to condition on electronic structure, steering atom arrangements toward desired properties.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research details Earth AI geospatial agents that combine planetary foundation models with reasoning to answer complex environmental and Earth-science questions.

items.title: He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art
items.excerpt: Moritz Hardt, author of a new book on benchmarks, argues AI's 'standardized tests' are fundamentally broken but fixable, and lays out a science of evaluation.

items.title: Claude just found a CRISPR-like DNA pattern, but even Anthropic's scientists aren't sure what it does
items.excerpt: Anthropic's Claude took less than a day to identify a curious CRISPR-like stretch of DNA; even Anthropic's scientists are not yet sure what it does.

items.title: Can AI break encryption? OpenAI's new math has cryptographers divided
items.excerpt: OpenAI's bumper crop of 722 AI-generated math papers wowed and worried researchers, and cryptographers are split over whether the algorithms protecting texts and bank logins are next.

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: Experiments show people draw a sharp line between human and AI consciousness: even when an AI behaves identically to a human, participants rate it as less conscious.

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: AI uncovered nearly 10,000 reactions in CO2-to-fuel conversion on copper catalysts, revealing pathways traditional models missed and sharply improving predictions.

items.title: Physicists develop early warning system that predicts when an AI is about to go rogue
items.excerpt: Physicists propose a mathematical formula that tracks an AI's internal 'compass needle' to flag undesirable outputs before they happen.

items.title: Can math stay human in the age of AI?
items.excerpt: As AI churns out mathematical proofs, a DeepMind study raises a bigger question: what is lost when mathematicians focus only on the answers?
